newsitem.title: UK: British royal yacht Britannia is to be replaced.
newsitem.headline: British royal yacht Britannia is to be replaced.

text.p: Britain announced on Wednesday it would build a new royal yacht costing 60 million pounds ($100 million) to replace Britannia in time for Queen Elizabeth's Golden Jubilee in 2002.
Britannia sailed on Monday on its final voyage and is to be taken out of service later this year after 44 years afloat.

The question of whether to replace Britannia has sparked a fierce debate between pragmatists, who say Britain can no longer afford expensive symbols of its past glories, and traditionalists, who see it as a priceless advertisement of all that is best about Britain.
Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, speaking for the latter, said the new ship would be "a symbol of the nation's pride".
"The vessel will be a symbol of the crown, the kingdom and its maritime traditions," he told parliament.
"It will be designed to exhibit an enduring level of style, elegance and dignity appropriate to its role, and should act as a showcase for Britain's design and engineering skills."
The last voyage of Britannia, a sleek 6,000-tonne, luxurious mini-liner with a crew of 234 and a Royal Marines band on board, is to mark the sun setting on British rule in Hong Kong.

Portillo said the new yacht would be built in British shipyards, creating up to 500 jobs, and would be paid for out of public funds. Among the proposals for a replacement is one for a three-masted sailing ship which could double as a youth training vessel when not being used by the queen or for trade promotion.
Private financing, he said, would not have been appropriate for a ship meant to provide the queen with a suitable residence when overseas and to project Britain's economic interests.
The queen will be consulted on the design and will contribute to the furnishings and fittings of the State Rooms and Royal Apartments.

Official spokesmen for the main opposition Labour party, perhaps sensing that the announcement was likely to be popular with voters, levelled their main criticism at the government's failure to consult on the decision.
But some Labour left-wingers, alluding to the royal family's colourful recent history, attacked the government.

"There is a language of priorities which says we shouldn't spend any more money on this aristocracy that's been pushing their own self-destruction button in the course of this past decade," Labour member of parliament Dennis Skinner said.

Although Britannia costs 10 million pounds a year to run, British exporters say the vessel is a unique asset that has more than paid its way by helping to secure two billion pounds ($3.35 billion) of exports for Britain over the past decade.
"It is able to attract a very high-quality trade audience. When the royal yacht sits in a harbour, people want to come aboard," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of banking giant Barclays.

Heir to the throne Prince Charles, who as a child holidayed aboard Britannia and also used it on his honeymoon with Princess Diana, is to sail out of Hong Kong a few minutes after midnight on July 1, when the colony is handed back to China.
Portillo said the government had decided not to sell Britannia to a private owner but was open to proposals for a suitably prestigious use for the ship in Britain.
